blocks.text: A capacitor does not allow direct current to pass through it because of the presence of an insulating medium between its plates. But alternating current can pass through a capacitor. In electric circuits, a capacitor is a reactive component. Unlike a resistor, a capacitor behaves differently in AC and DC circuits. It is because a capacitor can store energy in the form of electric field, whereas a resistor cannot store electrical energy in any form. Consider an alternating voltage source V is applied to a capacitor of capacitance C as shown in Fig.17.8 (a).

When an alternating voltage is applied across the plates of a capacitor, it is charged in one direction and then in the other as the voltage reverses. The result is that electrons move to and fro around the circuit, connecting the plates, thus, constituting alternating current. blocks.text: Father of ALTERNATING CURRENTS? Nikola Tesla was born in 1856 in Austria-Hungary and emigrated to the U.S.A. in 1884 as a physicist. He pioneered the generation, transmission, and use of alternating current which can be transmitted over much greater distances than direct current.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Equations 17.18 and 17.19 are for the capacitor: it is the capacitor current I that leads the voltage by 90°. In an inductor the current lags behind the voltage (Section 17.6).
